title: Primitives Stability Upgrade Runbook
body:
Purpose:
This runbook is a pragmatic, step-by-step guide for performing non-breaking upgrades and refactors of Terraform primitives used in Private Deployments (VPC, IAM, and Kubernetes primitives for EKS/GKE/AKS). It is focused on minimizing blast radius for customers running Private (VPC or on-prem) clusters, ensuring safe state transitions, and providing clear testing and rollback gates.

Scope:
- Modules covered: vpc, subnet, nat/gateway, iam-roles, oidc-provider, eks-cluster, gke-cluster, aks-cluster, nodepool primitives.
- State backends: S3/terraform-state with locking, GCS, and on-prem artifact registries.
- Targets: hosted/private deployments across cloud and air-gapped on-prem installs.

High-level upgrade strategy (principles):
1) Keep old outputs/inputs stable for one release cycle. Introduce v2 properties under new names instead of changing existing ones in-place.
2) Provide compatibility shims inside modules that translate legacy variables to new internal shapes.
3) Use compatibility outputs (e.g., vpc_id and vpc_id_v2) for transition; do not remove legacy outputs until consumers are migrated.
4) Staged rollout: canary (single tenant), bulk canary (subset of internal tenants), staged progressive rollouts by region/cluster, global.
5) Maintain automation to detect drift and validate plan-level diffs before applying.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Module Author: implements module changes, adds compatibility layer and tests.
- Release Owner: coordinates rollout windows and approves canaries.
- SRE/Oncall: monitors canary, ready to rollback.
- Solutions Eng: runs customer-facing canaries for enterprise customers.

Versioning policy (quick summary):
- Module tag format: vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (e.g., v1.4.2).
- Backwards-compatible additions -> bump MINOR. Breaking changes -> bump MAJOR and require two-release transition where v2 is published alongside v1 with explicit migration guide.
- Patch releases only for bug fixes.

Interface contract rules (inputs & outputs):
- Inputs: never rename a stable input in the same MAJOR series. If renaming is unavoidable, keep the old input and document it as deprecated; map it to the new name internally.
- Outputs: keep existing output names for at least one MINOR cycle after introducing replacements. Add new outputs with _v2 suffix (example: private_subnets -> private_subnets_v2).
- Sensitive values: mark as sensitive in outputs and avoid printing in logs. Use KMS/HSM for distribution on private installs.

Signals and health checks for a rollout:
- Plan parity: CI must produce a 0-diff plan for unaffected customers, and a human-reviewed plan for canaries.
- Smoke tests: cluster kube-system pods healthy within X minutes, node pools reporting ready, OIDC provider reachable, and IAM policy simulations pass for key roles.
- Cost/size regression: compare expected resource counts in plan (no accidental new resources).
- E2E: deploy a sample pod that uses the new primitives (ingress, mount, node selector) and assert success.

Backward compatibility guarantees (what we commit to):
- No implicit renames or output removal in a minor patch.
- Default behavior preserved unless explicitly overridden via a new flag.
- Terraform state renames: any state name changes must be accompanied by a documented terraform state mv recipe.

Testing & CI requirements (module authors must add):
- Unit: terratest or similar for resource shapes (mocked cloud).
- Plan guard: run terraform plan with the module pinned to old and new version; capture and diff plans automatically. Flag unexpected destroys.
- Integration sandbox: spin up a small cluster using the module in a sandbox AWS/GCP/Azure account; run smoke harness.
- State migration tests: add a pipeline job that runs terraform state mv commands against a snapshot state (stored test workspace) to validate commands.

State migration & operational commands (examples):
- Pin old version in consumer: module "vpc" { source = "git::https://...//modules/vpc?ref=v1.9.0" }
- Add new variables with defaults that reflect old behavior: variable "enable_new_subnet_scheme" { type = bool default = false }
- To move state key when changing module address: terraform state mv module.old_vpc.aws_vpc.my_vpc module.new_vpc.aws_vpc.my_vpc
- For provider namespace changes: terraform state mv "module.old.module.submodule.aws_iam_role.role" "module.new.module.submodule.aws_iam_role.role"
- If resource renames cannot be avoided, provide import scripts and example import commands in the PR.

Example upgrade sequence (recommended):
0) Preflight: run plan-diff pipeline and publish expected plan to release ticket.
1) Create feature branch and bump module tag to v2 (or v1.x+ if non-breaking).
2) Implement compatibility variables and outputs. Add deprecation warnings in module README and release notes.
3) Run CI: unit + plan-diff + integration sandbox.
4) Merge to main and publish module artifact to private registry / tag repo.
5) Canary rollout: update a single non-critical stack to reference the new module. Apply during low-traffic window. Monitor for 2X provisioning windows and pod restarts.
6) Validate canary: smoke tests pass for 30–60 minutes, no unexpected plan diffs on subsequent runs.
7) Bulk canary: roll forward to 10–20% of stacks (by customer or region).
8) Full rollout: proceed region-by-region with standard monitoring and oncall.
9) Deprecation: after all consumers migrated, schedule removal of legacy output names in the next major release.

Rollback plan (if canary fails):
- If a plan produced unexpected destroy/replace of customer-visible resources: abort apply, revert consumer change to previous module version and apply.
- If post-apply regressions occur: pin consumer to previous module tag, run terraform apply to restore previous resource shapes.
- If state is partially migrated: engage infra oncall to run manual terraform state mv reversals from backed-up state snapshots.

On-prem and air-gapped specifics:
- Module delivery: publish tarballs with SHA256 to internal artifact server. Provide 'registry_mirror' instructions in README.
- Terraform providers: ensure provider binaries are bundled or accessible in the air-gapped environment (document provider_version pinning).
- Secrets: use customer KMS/HSM; do not embed private keys in module artifacts.
- Upgrade window: coordinate with customer, schedule maintenance, and provide a migration checklist (local restore points, etc.).

EKS/GKE/AKS primitive notes (gotchas & recommendations):
- EKS: prefer outputting cluster_name, cluster_endpoint, cluster_ca_cert_base64, and node_group_names. Keep kubeconfig generation as opt-in in module (do not force writing kubeconfig to disk in private deployments).
- GKE: outputs should include private_cluster_config, node_locations, and workload_identity_pool_id (if using WIF).
- AKS: avoid exposing managed identity secrets; output principal IDs and role assignment ids instead.
- OIDC providers: when rotating OIDC configuration, create new provider resource and keep the old one until all roles trust the new issuer.
- IAM roles: add versioned role names or tags (role_name_v2) during migration to avoid immediate name collisions when both old and new sets coexist.

Variable naming guidelines (practical list):
- Keep names short and explicit: vpc_id, private_subnets, public_subnets, nat_gateway_ids, cloud_region.
- New variables should be suffixed with _v2 for major redesigns.
- Avoid boolean flags that invert behavior without clear name (prefer enable_new_foo = true over old_style = false).

Outputs & selectors pattern (safe evolution):
- When changing the shape from id -> list(map), add a new output and keep the old one. Example: private_subnets (list) and private_subnets_map_v2 (list(object(...))).
- Provide lightweight helpers in README: a sample locals block that adapts new output to old consumers if they need it.

Checklist for module PRs that perform interface changes:
- [ ] Add compatibility variables with clear defaults.
- [ ] Add new outputs with _v2 suffix; keep legacy outputs.
- [ ] Add terratest cases and a plan-diff CI job.
- [ ] Add terraform state mv recipe if resource addresses change.
- [ ] Update README with migration steps and example consumer changes.
- [ ] Run integration sandbox and attach test logs to PR.
- [ ] Tag a release and publish artifact with release notes.

Open questions / unresolved items (to discuss in follow-up):
- Decommission periods: what is the guaranteed minimum window between deprecation and removal for enterprise customers? (proposal: 90 days).
- Should we standardize a single transitional output suffix (_v2) or allow contextual names?
- State snapshot automation: can we automate snapshot/restore for each canary application in a reproducible way for faster rollback?

Appendix: quick commands and troubleshooting tips:
- Run plan diff against pinned old module: TF_LOG=info ./ci/plan-diff.sh --old-ref v1.9.0 --new-ref v2.0.0
- Move state example: terraform state mv "module.old_vpc.aws_vpc.vpc" "module.new_vpc.aws_vpc.vpc"
- If apply stuck waiting for provider: check provider version pins and the provider mirror in the air-gapped registry.
- If node groups fail to join: check bootstrap userdata and instance profile role permissions; run aws eks describe-nodegroup / gcloud container clusters describe for diagnostics.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intended as a living runbook. Please comment on required monitoring metrics and add any proven smoke-test snippets you rely on.
- If you maintain downstream consumer stacks (solutions eng / customer success), add a short checklist for customer-facing communication when we schedule upgrades.

Last reviewed: 2025-01-12 by Aisha Malik (owner)
